title: The Theory of Forms
text:
Plato posited that true reality exists not in the observable physical world, but rather within an eternal, non-material realm called the Forms. These Forms represent the ideal blueprints for everything encountered in sensible experience—such as Justice itself, or Beauty itself—and are considered perfect and unchanging ideals.

The material objects perceived through the senses are viewed as mere imperfect copies or shadows of these ultimate Forms. Consequently, genuine knowledge (episteme) is not derived from fickle sensory perception but must instead be achieved through intellectual apprehension and pure reason alone. The mind's function is to grasp the stable structure of the Forms, thereby understanding the inherent order governing existence.
